utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar, and everybody. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. All the accused here. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. The Defence absentees are Mr. Nikolic, Ms. Nikolic, Mr. Krgovic, and Mr. Sarapa. All right. Let us get rid of this from our table. Mr. Lazarevic, Mr. Gosnell, you will recall your motion for admission of documents from the bar table filed on the 16th of October. You will also recall, Mr. McCloskey, that you filed your response on the 31st of October not objecting to such admission. We are, therefore, granting the motion. Mr. Zivanovic, I am sure that although it is Friday, you will still recall your motion of the 20th October, 2008, in which you asked the -- requested the Trial Chamber to grant you leave to file the motion for admission of evidence from the bar table at the end of your case, and that's in view of the decision of the Trial Chamber confirmed by the Appeals Chamber to reopen the Prosecution case and to hear the testimony of the communications expert, Mr. Rodic, during that stage of the proceedings and not during Miletic's case as now scheduled. The Prosecution responded on the 3rd of November and not objecting to your motion. In view of that, we hereby grant the motion. That disposes of two motions. Good morning to you, Professor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We were discussing, actually, whether there is a way --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- to try to finish with your testimony today, but I am not that optimistic. We'll try. We'll try. By the way, we'll be sitting as follows; there is a change in the schedule: We'll be sitting 90-minute sessions instead of 100-minute sessions, and we'll finish at 3.00 instead of half past 3. So the break, lunch break will be at 1.30 to -- from 12.30 to 1.30. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and good morning. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Dr. Ristivojevic. I would like to continue where we left it off.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't receiving interpretation, but the reason was I was on the wrong channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We already spoke in great detail about the way the criminal matter was regulated, and let's talk about the proceedings and legal matter, and how was that regulated in Republika Srpska from the year 1992 to the period that we had in mind, that is 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We said that at the level of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, there was a singular source of authority on the procedural legal matter; i.e., there was one law on legal proceedings. It was adopted by Republika Srpska in 1993 to the full with some minor changes, which were not important for my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's now go to 4D206, which is under your tab 10. And as for the rest, we will just mention them. This is the law on criminal procedure which was published on 30th December in 1993 in the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska. You've already told us that these amendments, the law on criminal procedure is something you did not consider too relevant for your report.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like in the Penal Code, these were the changes that -- and amendments that was due to hyperinflation. The value of the money was devaluated, and that's why periodically amendments were made to make adjustments to the new value of the currency.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now I am going to just mention them. The exhibits that contain certain amendments to the law on criminal procedure, these are 4D376 - I don't think that we should call them up on e-court - 4D376 is the first exhibit, and we also have 4D413, which refers to the application of the Law on Criminal Procedure in conditions of an immediate threat of war or state of war. In your expert, in paragraphs 36 and 37 of your report, you dealt with these documents that contained amendments. Did these amendments have any bearing on the topic of your expert report?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not have any specific bearing. One of the matters was the shortening of the deadlines in the criminal procedure given that there was a state of war. Some legal remedies were either added or abolished, but that all was not of any importance for my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, I would like to move on to the regulations that regulated the organisation of courts. And first of all, let's look at a document under your tab 12, which is -- I apologise. Its seems that I have been speaking too fast. The exhibit number is 4D373. This is a decision on the competence of courts in criminal matters, and the date on the document that you will see --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just repeat for the record. This is 20 May 1992. That's the date on the document. Let's look at Article 1 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what this law regulates in this article?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that lower courts have subject matter re: jurisdiction to conduct legal proceedings in the first instance. The lower courts would correspond to what is known as municipal courts in the neighbouring states, for example, in the state of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Under your tab 3 is the following document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 4D183. This is a Decision on the Establishment, Seat, and Jurisdiction of Military Courts and Military Prosecutor's Offices. Let's look at Article 1 of this decision first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is the wrong document, obviously, in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, I find it to be much easier for me to follow your question and evidence of the witness if you indicate what part of the report you are dealing with in addition to the exhibit numbers in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour. I'll try to organise this in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the decision before us. First of all, let's look at Article 1 of this decision. What does Article 1 regulate? Which courts are established hereby?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article deals primarily with the establishment of first instance military courts in Banja Luka, Sarajevo, and Bijeljina, as well as the supreme court in Sarajevo as a Court of appeal or second-instance court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to mention that these are paragraphs starting from 3.9 of the expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, let's look at paragraph 2 of this decision. Can you please tell me where were the regional military Prosecutor's offices established?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were established with the corps commands in the same cities where the first instance military courts were established, which means in Banja Luka, Sarajevo, and Bijeljina; and also, a senior military Prosecutor's Office was established with the Main Staff of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The name, the official name was the senior military Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I would like us to look at is under your tab 14, and this is exhibit number P420, the law on military Prosecutor's Offices, dated 13 December 1993. Could we please look at Article 1 of that law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It appears we don't have translation of this particular document. It was a P document, and we were of the impression that this whole law is translated in English, but it appears that only certain parts were translated, so I will go through relevant articles with the witness by reading portions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ristivojevic, can you now look at Article 1.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since, unfortunately, we don't have a translation of this article, could you please read Article 1 very slowly, and it will be recorded.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The military Prosecutor's office prosecutes perpetrators of crimes which are under the jurisdiction of military courts. It also undertakes certain measures to protect the interests of the community and uses legal means to protect the constitutionality and legality in the way prescribed by this law or other laws or regulations."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We've just read out from Article 1 of this law. It seems that this regulates the activity of the military Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I would say the jurisdiction of the military Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would like to ask you with regard to this law, there is another article that you deemed relevant for your report, and that is Article 7 on the same page under paragraph 2 entitled "Jurisdiction and Authority." Just for the record, could you please read Article 7?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The right and duty of the military Prosecutor's office is to prosecute perpetrators of crimes which are subject matter of military courts for which are prosecuted ex officio, and with this regard they are also duty-bound to do the following: Under 1, undertake the necessary measures to detect crimes as well as their perpetrators and to start the initial criminal proceedings; under 2, issues a request for criminal investigation to be carried out; under 3, issues the indictment and represents the state before the competent military court; and under 4, lodges an appeal against court decisions and also files the legal remedies against final court decisions." The next paragraph reads: "The military Prosecutor discharges other duties and exercise the other rights that are within his purview under the law."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What I wanted to ask you with this regard is this: This Article 7, is this the elaboration of the duties and authorities of the military Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a detailed elaboration of Article 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to move on in this document, P420, which also contains the Law on Military Courts that was issued on the 30th of December, 1993. We will be talking about paragraphs 3.11 to 3.14 of your expert report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the pages in e-court that I would like to call are 4 in B/C/S and page 1 in the English version of this document. Let's first look at Article 1 of this regulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In keeping with Article 1 of this regulation, how were military courts defined and regulated?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military courts are defined like regular courts as courts that shall try military personnel as well as other individuals for the criminal acts stipulated by this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's now move on to Article 8 of this law. Could you please tell me what this article defines?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It defines military personnel, and a reference is made here to the Law on the Military.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify this, let's please look at document 4D372, which is under your tab 15. This is the Law on the Army dated 1st June, 1992. I would like us to look at its Article 3, please. In keeping with Article 3 of the Law on the Army, which was referred to by the previous law with regard to the definition of military personnel, could you tell us how "military personnel" is defined according to Article 3 of the Law on the Army?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Article 3 of this law, the military personnel are the following: Soldiers, cadets at military academies, active members of the military, and reserve members of the military while on military duty in the army. The next paragraph of the same article defines active members of the military as officers, non-commissioned officers, and soldiers under contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I would like to go back to the Law on Military Courts, which is under your tab 14. This is P420.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up page 2 in both B/C/S and English versions of this document, and I would like us to look at Article 13 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe we have both documents in e-court. Can you tell me, what does Article 13 of this law stipulate, and can you please give us your interpretation?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the exemptions just like Article 1, which speaks about the jurisdiction of military court when it says certain crimes committed by other individuals can be tried by a military court as well. Therefore, Article 13 says that in the event of other individuals - called "civilians" here - act as co-perpetrators or accomplices of the perpetrator, they all fall under the jurisdiction of a military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In your report, you also made reference to articles 9 and 11, which stipulate the organisation and jurisdiction of military court, but would I would not like dwell on that particular part. However, let us look at Article 10, last paragraph. Can you tell us what Article 10 stipulates in its last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 5 in B/C/S and page 2 in English in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This paragraph of Article 10 lays down the jurisdiction of military courts to try all crimes committed against prisoners of war and the jurisdiction of military courts in terms of establishing the status of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the last that I would like to ask you with regard to this law is Article 56. It's on page 9 in B/C/S and page 8 in English in e-court -- I apologise, in English version. Paragraph 3 and 4 are of particular interest for this case. In what way does Article 56 define the entities that have jurisdiction pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Law on Criminal Procedure is applicable to a military court, as well, pursuant to the first paragraph of this article. In paragraph 2 of this article, individual jurisdictions are being governed pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure which are entrusted to certain procedural entities. According to paragraph 2, the duties and powers exercised in regular courts are -- within the purview of the Ministry of the Interior, when it comes to trials conducted by military courts, shall be afforded to security organs and the military police. The duties and powers of public prosecutors in the trials conducted before regular courts shall be afforded to military Prosecutors in the trials conducted by military courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether the MUP organs have any sort of power in the proceedings before military courts?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they do not. And I said this is pursuant to paragraph 2, as I said a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As for the content of the powers, they are described in more detail in paragraph 3.14 of your report. We are not going to go into that in detail, and it deals with the powers relating to the Law on Criminal Procedure. I would just like to draw the attention to the documents used in your report, which are 4D381 and 4D212, but we shall perhaps deal with that later. Now, let me ask you this: At the request of the Defence, you reviewed the indictment. I'm talking about paragraph 3.24 in your report. I am speaking particularly about the crime relating to the Kravica warehouse. The indictment states that the direct perpetrators of that act were members of the special police brigade, a member of the Bratunac Brigade, and one civilian. That's what the indictment says. Tell me, in this particular instance, which court would have exclusive jurisdiction to conduct a trial, a criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular situation, exemptions stipulated by Article 13 would be applied, and I'm referring to the Law on the Military Courts. Given that in this group of individuals cited as direct perpetrators of this crime, there were military personnel involved or, rather, one member of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the court that would have jurisdiction would be which?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most definitely a military court would have jurisdiction. And, of course, the military Prosecutor's office would be in charge of prosecuting the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we define the territorial jurisdiction of a military court in this situation?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, the territorial jurisdiction would be that of the military court in Bijeljina. However, I have to put forward a reservation pursuant to Article 9 of the Law on Military Courts. Territorial jurisdiction of military courts is determined by the president of the republic at the proposal of the Minister of Defence. I have not received this law within the materials that I had reviewed; and therefore, I was unable to establish precisely the territorial jurisdiction of respective military courts. My conclusion in my report was drawn on the basis of the territory covered by the indictment. The closest military court in this case was the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, would the MUP organs have any powers in preliminary proceedings and criminal proceedings conducted by a military court?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of which military court we are talking about, the one in Bijeljina or any other court, members of the MUP would not have any powers or jurisdiction in criminal proceedings. As we said, these powers and this jurisdiction in criminal proceedings conducted by military courts are -- fall within the remit of security organs and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Right. Let us now move on to a part of your report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, if you exhausted this issue. Professor Ristivojevic, if there had been no military that participated in Kravica, for example, what court would have had the jurisdiction then, if the crimes were -- had been committed only by this special police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to item 38 on the application of the Laws on War --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... what page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please give me a moment to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. It's P409, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just see. That's P409. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's tab 30 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 37 speaks only about military personnel by saying that military courts have jurisdiction over them. Article 38 introduces the jurisdiction of military courts for all perpetrators. That's how it reads. It makes no distinction between various statuses of individuals. It further says that the proceedings are going to be conducted according to the law on military procedure, the Law on the Military Prosecutor's Office, and the Law on Military Courts, and finally, the Law on Military Courts during the state of an immediate threat of war or war. In the Law on Military Courts, there is no explicit stipulation of the jurisdiction of military courts relating to non-military personnel, but rather, this jurisdiction is laid down under Article 38 of these regulations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure Professor Ristivojevic followed my question, and I don't think P409 is the relevant material. Professor, my question was what court, civil or military court, would have had jurisdiction if these certain crimes are committed only by the police, special police resubordinated or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I'm not talking about resubordination. These regulations were drawn in 1978, and they relate to military personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So put it simply. You talked about the example of Kravica house. According to the indictment, there were one military personnel who participated. Because of that, you said the military court would have had jurisdiction. If he was not there, what court would have the jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat, the Law on Military Courts explicitly introduces this jurisdiction but only when it refers to non-military personnel. We would have to construe these acts. Article 38 refers to military personnel. In 1992, the president of the Republika Srpska issued an order on the application of the Rules of Laws of War applicable to members of the police and the military as well. In other words, he introduced in the armed forces of Republika Srpska. Therefore, my conclusion was that all members of the armed forces were under the jurisdiction of military courts in the event of the breach of international law. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Laws of war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, we need interpretation of these regulations because at the time when these regulations were adopted in 1988 [Realtime transcript read in error, "1978"], police was not part of the armed forces [as interpreted]; only the army and the Territorial Defence were part of the armed forces. In 1992, the president of Republika Srpska equalised the police and members of the army and afforded them an equal status of member of armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. We have a minor problem with the transcript. It's page 14, lines 5 and 6. You were talking about the year 1988, whereas it says here 1978.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's when the laws on the application of the laws of war were adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you also were talking about members of the armed forces rather than of military personnel, as it is said here. Well, I think we've cleared that up now, and I'd like to move on to another area or, rather, a continuation of what we've been discussing. Paragraphs 325 to 327 of your expert report, which is to be found on pages 21 and 22 in the B/C/S version and page 16 of the English. And there, you refer to the decision to proclaim an immediate threat of war and state of war, and documents are mentioned there, 4D527, P425, and 42219 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat these numbers more slowly, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you need to repeat the numbers more slowly please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. I'll repeat that. The documents that we -- or rather, you used in your report are 4D527, P425, and 4D219, and we're relating to paragraphs 3.25 to 3.27 [Realtime transcript read in error, "325 to 327"] of your expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'd just like us to take a look first of all -- 3.25 and 3.27 are the last numbers of the paragraphs there. Yes. That's how it should be now. It's been recorded properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, let's just look at P425 first on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's tab 22 in your set of documents. It's a Decision on the Declaration of a State of War in the Skelani Municipality of the 14th of July, 1995. This document is self-explicit; it's self-evident, but just to note the time. When on the Srebrenica-Skelani municipality a state of war was in fact proclaimed, can you tell us the date?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me by looking at point 6 of this decision what it regulates with respect to the state of immediate threat of war?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state of the immediate threat of war ceases to be effective with the passing of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, I'd like us to look at a few documents which came before this particular document, the one we've just been looking at, and it is in your -- in tab 24 of your report, and it is a document numbered P10.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we have that put up on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is a decision to appoint a civilian commissar for the Srpska-Srebrenica municipality dated the 11th of July, 1995; and I'd like to look at point 4 of this decision, to appoint a civilian commissioner. Does it give authorisation to the civilian commissioner with respect to the treatment of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. According to point 4, the commissioner shall ensure that those who fought against the army of Republika Srpska, such persons should have -- should be treated as prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, if we look at the next point, point 5, which says decisions by the civilian commissioner shall be binding for all civilian authority organs in these Serbian municipality of Srebrenica, my first question in that relationship is this: To whom are these -- to whom is this binding?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I understand this point in the following way, that the civilian organs of authority, that is to say state administration and similar organs, are duty-bound to follow the decisions of the civilian commissioner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And now purely territorially, let's see what this is all about. What territory does this refer to, what municipality?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the title says it all. It says the decision refers to the Serbian municipality of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Thank you. And while we're on this topic, may we take a look at the next document which you have in your binder. It is number 25, and it is document 4D379, which is a decision on the appointment of the War Presidency for Srebrenica municipality, Skelani, of the 14th of July, 1995; and it was published in the Official Gazette in August 1995. Tell me now, please, when the War Presidency was being established for the Srebrenica-Skelani municipality, did that mean that the authorisations of the civilian commissioner ceased to be effective, the civilian commissioner that we talked about a moment ago and his powers and authority?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how I understand the relationship between these two decisions. When the new appointments were made, they meant that all previous authorisations ceased to be effective.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we are, of course, referring to the territory on which the state of war was proclaimed, and we've already had an opportunity to see this on the basis of document P425; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to the Srebrenica-Skelani municipality in the heading of this document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. And while we're on the subject of the proclamation of the state of war, I'd like us to look at the next document, which in your documents, in your -- documents, it'll be found in tab 26. And it is document 4D525, the Law on the application of the law of governing military courts and the military Prosecutor's office during a state of war, and perhaps we could look at Article 2 there. Can you tell me what Article 2 of this law stipulates?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 2 of this law stipulates the following: That during a state of war, so-called military courts for special wartime situations may be convened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, let's look at Article 4 and what that article stipulates. Let's look at paragraph 1 first and then paragraph 2. Can you tell us what that provides for?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It provides for the fact that the military Prosecutor during a state of war has the same authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What does paragraph 2 of the article state?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stipulates, as was set out in the previous article, that in proceedings before a military court, when there's a state of war, the security organs and the military police shall have the same authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Let's now move on to Article 8, para 2 of this law. Who, according to this article, has the authority to set up special military courts? There are two terms used there, "a military court for special situations" and "extraordinary military courts." Are they the same courts?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is one and the same court in Article 8, and for some reason the legislator used two terms. But it is my opinion that it is one and the same court, which is always an extraordinary court as is stipulated in Article 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And who is in charge of establishing this extraordinary military court?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this article, it is established or convened through an order by the commander of the unit of the level of a brigade or regiment along with agreement from the corps commander -- with prior agreement by the corps commander, or that court can be established by the corps commander himself or, rather, the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to Article 10 now of this law and look at paragraph 3 of Article 10, which provides for the possibility of the court trying employees of the Ministry of the Interior. Now, where do you see the importance of this particular provision?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This provision explicitly states or speaks about the authority of the court-martials or extraordinary courts for members of the Ministry of the Interior and determines and stipulates that the trial chamber of such a court-martial shall include on the panel of judges there should be a member of the command of that particular MUP unit to which the policeman being tried belongs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to say that in paragraphs 3.29 to 3.32 of your expert report deals with this particular topic. Now, let us look at another document, which is related to the court-martials, and it is tab 27 of your documents, and it is document 6D166. It is an order by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS dated the 30th of July, 1995. And I'd like us to look at page 3, point 17, which is to be found on page 4 of the English version. Tell me now, please, what is the importance of point 17 as you see it, the -- with respect to the establishment of court-martials for extraordinary military courts?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point 17 in itself is more of a declarative nature rather than stipulating a law to follow, and that means that it lends impetus to the duty -- it reinforces the duty which the officers have with respect to setting up a military court and court-martials, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to court-martials, these extraordinary courts, you have had an opportunity of analysing quite a number of documents. Did you come across any information according to which a court-martial either at the level of a regiment, brigade, corps or Main Staff was in fact set up? Have you found a document with an example like that which would confirm that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the documents that I reviewed, my answer would be no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us look at another document, one more document which is linked to this topic. It is in tab 28 of your documents, and it is document 4D357 which is a document of the MUP of Republika Srpska dated the 18th of August, 1995. And I'd like us to look at paragraph 3 of that particular document which begins with the words "pursuant to the provisions of Article 2 of the Law on Implementation of the Law on Defence ..." Tell me now, please, what does this document say in relation to the subject we've been discussing, that is to say the possibility of having court-martials try persons belonging to the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior pursuant to this document reminds all members of the ministry that they are part of the armed forces. It also reminds them of the possibility of establishing special military courts in special circumstances. Why? Well, because those courts -- those court-martials can make only -- can issue only one sentence, and that is the death sentence, and I assume that the minister feels bound to emphasize this to the members of the ministry of the authority of these courts and their right on the panel of judges or Trial Chamber of such a court-martial, that one -- at least one judge -- or rather, one judge should be from the command of the unit to which the person being tried belongs, that is to say, the policeman being tried belongs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. [In English] The translation, that reference was made to this court as extraordinary military court or court-martial, so just to make sure that we are talking about one and the same court, just in order to have this in transcript. [Interpretation] Very well. I would like us to move on to the next chapter of your report, which refers to the responsibilities in respect of the international humanitarian law and treatment of prisoners of war. You already told us that the law of Republika Srpska envisaged all the rights ensuing from the international humanitarian law and law on customs of war.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in chapter 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next document that I would like us to see is P28, and in your binder it is under tab 29. These are the guidelines to determine criteria for criminal prosecution, which were compiled by the military Prosecutor's Office affiliated with the Main Staff of the VRS in October 1992. You've already had an occasion to analyse this document, and you have mentioned it in your expert report. What is the nature of this document in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to its legal nature, I should say that this document, firstly, repeats and reiterates and then additionally elaborates the already-existing law. In other words, its primary intention is to explain to those who will be involved in criminal prosecution, the elements of the crimes that they are supposed to prosecute. The purpose of the document, as it says in its heading, is to -- unification of the policies of criminal prosecution - that's part of the heading - and the introduction of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who is this the document intended for primarily? What was your conclusion when you first saw this act?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is primarily intended for the military judiciary his, as it says in the introduction, and the document goes on to break down and say the officers, the military officers, the officers in charge of units and institutions, the military police, security organs, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's now look at just one portion of this document on page 15 and on page 16. First of all, can we please look at the very end of page 15 and the beginning of page 16 in your copy, and we're talking about pages 31 and 33 in e-court; and in English, the page numbers are 7 and 8. And now we can see the parts starting with "all commands of the units are duty-bound to ..." So whose obligation was it to implement the procedures to detect crimes against humanity and international laws in keeping with these guidelines? Please focus on pages 15 and 16.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these guidelines, the unit commands are duty-bound to work on the detection of cases that involve crimes against humanity and the international law in their respective zones of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who should be informed or conveyed information about any such crimes detected in keeping with these guidelines?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a crime is detected and illucidated, according to these guidelines, it is the organs of the military police that should be informed, the security organs, and the military judiciary organs that should be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am going to be moving on to a slightly different topic. If we can have a break right now and then proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because we do have a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We prefer if you could start with the other topic, and then we stop at 10.30 as scheduled, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And now, I would like us to move on to a new document, which is the regulations on the implementation of the international laws in the SFRY. It's under your tab 30, and it is Exhibit number P409. So the implementation of the law -- war law. Let's look at chapter 2, item 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is on page 16 in B/C/S, and in the English version, it is page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the title of this chapter is "The Responsibility for the Acts Committed by Subordinates." My question to you about this item 21 is this: Does it make the officer of the unit of the Ministry of the Interior responsible if such a unit was resubordinated to a VRS unit in combat?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 21 of this regulation speaks about the military officers as persons who are responsible for the violations of the law on the customs of war. If we were to dwell upon a strict linguistic interpretation, we may find ourselves in a situation which seems to be illogical to a certain extent, at least to me. It would seem that only military officers would be deemed responsible for the acts committed by their subordinates as has been regulated by this item 21. And that at the same time, there are some other types of commanders, for example, police commanders, who would not have the same responsibility for the acts comitted by their subordinates. That would actually introduce two different standards in the war law. It seems to me that the strict linguistic interpretation should not be applicable here because it is wrong. What should be the only criteria -- criterion for the interpretation of this regulation is the fact that -- that a certain commander has subordinates, i.e., men under his command to whom he issues orders or not. It seems to me that the proper way to interpret this provision should be to the -- for this regulation to also make the police unit commander responsible for the acts of his subordinates. In my view, this would be the only logical interpretation of this regulation. By applying pure linguistic interpretation, we would end up with a rather illogical solution. There is one more reason why a pure logical interpretation should not be used here, is the fact that in 1988 when these regulations were passed, the police was not part of the armed forces, and that very fact shows that the legislator was not forced to look at the police commander when drafting this law. It is very difficult for me to believe that the proper interpretation would be only linguistic and that the only persons that would be relevant here would be only military commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Obviously, we are talking about the year 1995, and you've already told us that the regulations were passed in 1988?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And that the Law on National Defence, i.e., the law on Defence which was passed on the 29 November, 1994, the units of the Ministry of the Interior became part of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, and that was made official at the time?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the validity of the provisions of the international war law was adopted even sooner. The president of Republika Srpska extended those provisions to the members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about compliance with the provisions of the international war law?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are talking about that, and we are talking about the application of this law on police members as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to analyse Article 21 and break it down into three parts. We are talking about the commander of a police unit resubordinated to the commander of the unit in whose area of responsibility such a unit is engaged in combat. What would be the responsibilities or the obligations of such a commander when they learned that their subordinates are prepared to commit an act that constitutes a violation of the international war law?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that he should undertake measures in order to prevent such violations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's now look at a different situation. What would be the responsibility or obligation of a -- the commander of a police unit who were to catch his subordinate red-handed in the commission of an act that constitutes a violation of the war law?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 21 does not specify anything about the very commission of such an act, but the only logical interpretation that arises from the fact that the military officer is duty-bound to prevent any violation of the provisions of the war law which is underway, so obviously it arises from that, that they would be duty-bound to prevent any violation of the war law underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, just one more situation. If the commander of such a unit -- let me first ask you this: Would the commander of such a unit, and we are referring to a unit of the Ministry of the Interior resubordinated to a military unit, would such a commander be in charge of launching the proceedings of instituting an investigation, would such a commander be in charge and responsibile for that in a situation like this?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the instigation of criminal proceedings, there is no responsibility for that. Such responsibilities are regulated clearly by the Law on Criminal -- on Military Courts, as we have already said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And what would be the obligation of an officer who is not responsibility for investigating -- instigating an investigation? We're talking about the same situation.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last sentence in the first paragraph speaks about that very clearly. He would be a -- responsible and duty-bound to report the perpetrator to the military officer in charge, and I quote from the text of the regulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I understand you wish to have the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, now it's time, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, we'll have a 30-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Ristivojevic, while we are still on paragraph 21, I would like to ask you a few more questions regarding this. You already spoke about the linguistic and logical interpretations. Generally speaking, how a commander of a police unit or a commanding officer fits into the definition and provisions contained in paragraph 21?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, the very fact that a commander has certain men subordinated to him, something that should stem from that fact is his obligation with regard to the procedure and the acts comitted by his subordinates if they are -- indeed, they are subordinates, if he is entitled the issue orders to them. In that case, the interpretation of the provisions of item 21 should, in my opinion, be such that a police unit commander should undertake measures to prevent acts committed by his subordinate which constitute breaches of the laws of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is the situation or, rather, the obligations of a commander with regard to those who are not his subordinates? Does he have the same obligations?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, concerning the individuals who are not his subordinates and to whom he cannot issue orders, such an obligation would not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wondered if my colleague could clarify just for the record whether or not the answer that was given in relation to his last question related only to this particular document or provision or was a more general question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was a more general question. My colleague can, of course, operate in his cross-examination he wishes to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, this subject has been dealt with in paragraph 4.7 to 4.8 in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 4.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, who has jurisdiction in this situation to conduct proceedings i.e., the situation in which an officer is not empowered to conduct such proceedings, of course, if faced with the violation of the international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question? I am not sure I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at item 38 of these regulations. You already spoke about this. Let us just establish who has the jurisdiction to conduct proceedings pursuant to item 38.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is military courts who have jurisdiction to conduct proceedings for the violations of the international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look now at item 51 on page 25 in B/C/S and also page 25 in English in e-court. Can you tell me, pursuant to item 51, what are the duties of members of the armed forces when they capture members of the enemy armed forces?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with item 51, they are duty-bound to spare their lives and to treat them humanely. At the same time, this item provides an obligation for members of the armed forces to prevent the prisoner from escaping and to undertake all measures with a view to taking the prisoner to a safe facility as soon as possible and hand it over to a designated officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is the situation concerning any other individual taken prisoner in a combat zone?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to item 51, they should be treated in the same fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to item 51, who has the jurisdiction to establish the identity and the status of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to paragraph 2 of this item, specially designated military organs have these powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do we have an explicit definition of these organs?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not under this item.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to item 213 of these regulations. It's on page 57 in B/C/S and page 63 in English. It's entitled "The Initial Capturing," and it's called 2 -- and item 213 is entitled "Capture." Pursuant to this item, what are the obligations of officers with respect to the safety of their own unit when they are in the process of capturing members of the enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with paragraph 2 of this item, the officer shall take all measures of precaution in order to ensure the safety and security of his unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How do you understand "...undertakes the measures to ensure the safety and security of his own unit"?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This item does not elaborate in detail what these measures specifically are, but rather, says "all measures," and I'm quoting, "all measures of precaution."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: The provisions of item 213, are they applicable to MUP members or a commander of a MUP unit in a situation when they are resubordinated to a military unit in which the zone of responsibility they carry out tasks?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this item establishes an obligation incumbent on such an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now move on to item 217 of these regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on page 58 in B/C/S and on page 64 in English. It governs the issues of evacuation of POWs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when POWs are evacuated, in what situations?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this item, immediately upon capture, the POWs - as it says here - must be evacuated from the combat zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The lists of POWs are to what point regulated according to this item as something that has to be done?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either during the evacuation itself or until their arrival in a camp outside the danger zone at the latest. This is when the lists of evacuees, POW evacuees should be compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at the next document dealing with the same matter. I would just like to mention that this whole subject --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the numbers of the items again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, the interpreters would like you to repeat the number of the items again. If you look at the transcript, you see exactly where they couldn't follow you, lines 2 and 3 on page 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This whole area is covered by items 4.11 to 4.21 in your expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document 4D184 in e-court, and that's an instruction on how to treat POWs dated 13th of July, 1992. It was published in the Official Gazette of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's your tab number 31. In your view, what does this document represent?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order issued by the president of the republic on the application and observance of the Law of War by the Armed Forces. The Minister of Defence is thereby instructed to issue such guidelines, and these are these instructions or the guidelines signed by the Minister of Defence in June 1992; and therefore, he had fulfilled his obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like us to look at point 1 of this set of instructions, and could you tell us what that regulates?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I regulates the following: That in dealing with captured persons, the treatment of captured persons, the rights and duties pursuant to these instructions incumbent upon members of the army and members of the police force, they apply to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at point 4 -- 4.1 of these instructions, or para 1. It says there that: "Captured persons shall be taken to reception centres as determined by a senior officer with the rank of company commander or by a person holding an equal or higher position before the start of combat activities." Tell me now, please, in view of this provision, does it relate to the officer of the MUP unit who is resubordinated to the unit and the area of responsibility of that unit?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, this provision should be interpreted in the following way: It should be understood that it is binding upon the officer with the rank of company commander or by a person holding an equal or higher position in the army and not as applying to the police because the planning and preparation of combat activities is something that comes under the army's remit, not the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like us to go through some more documents referring to prisoners of war, and the first document is in tab 32 in your papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is P3035, document P3035, a document of the Drina Corps command dating the 15th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's just take a look at the bottom half of this document, which is point 2 or para 2, and it starts with the words "With the aim of strengthening responsibility ..." et cetera. What is your interpretation of the importance of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I feel that paragraph 2 of this document, in order to strengthen responsibility, et cetera, is of a declarative nature, just like some of the ones we saw earlier on, the purpose of which is to raise the level of awareness about the need to respect war law. Furthermore, this document instructs the units to elect persons within the units who are going to study the provisions of International War Law and making them the soldiers in the army familiar with those provisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Now, let's look at the next document. It is tab 33 in your set.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is document P3034.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to come up on e-court, it is another set of instructions to the Bratunac Brigade about conduct with prisoners of war of the 17th of July, 1993. Quite obviously, this is two days after the previous document that we were just looking at, so this is a document issued two days later. Let's look at the bottom half of the document first, and it is the last paragraph beginning with the words: "Each prisoner of war should be isolated and taken to a place of safety and guarded and then inform the command of the brigade and ask the military police to take over the prisoners." Now, let's go on to the second page of this document and look at the first paragraph there, which begins: "During the time that prisoners spend in the military police and come under the jurisdiction of the security organs, humane conditions should be furnished," et cetera, et cetera. Tell me now, please, we've just seen this document, so under whose authority do the prisoners of war come as can be deduced from this set of instructions from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These instructions were compiled in order to put into effect the previous one and -- concerning the Drina Corps, as is stated in paragraph 1, and on -- in paragraph 1 of page 2 of these instructions, the prisoners, as it says, during their stay in the military police facilities come under the jurisdiction of the security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the next document is to be found in tab 34 of your set of documents, and it is instructions of the security administration about the arrest and escorting of prisoners of war dated the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is document P196. I'd like us to look at page 2 of that document, point 2 of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, in keeping with this document, who determines the locality at which the POWs are to be collected in?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, the Drina Corps command, the localities behind the front where POWs are to be collected is determined by the commands from battalion level upwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who provides their security and interrogates POWs?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on in this paragraph, we see that the location where POWs are collected must be such that the prisoners are fully secured as well as the people from the security organ, from the intelligence organ and military police organ, engaging in interrogation and guarding the POWs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now the next document I'd like us to look at is tab 36 in your set, and it is P3025. It is an order for active combat activities of the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade dated the 5th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have page 5 displayed of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You can see there that it says the area of collection for POWs, and Pribicevac is mentioned. Is that in keeping with the previous set of instructions issued that we looked at a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is. And according to this order, as it says, The security organs, military police shall determine the location for the collection of POWs and their security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, bearing in mind all the legal provisions that we've looked at so far as well as these documents, and there are some more documents that you deal with when writing your expert report, on the basis of all that, can you tell us what your position is with respect to the responsibilities of the Ministry of the Interior vis-a-vis prisoners of war, and I mean specifically to the members of the Ministry of the Interior taking part in combat activities and are resubordinated to the military command in whose area of responsibility these combat activities are taking place?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All members of the armed forces are duty-bound by International War Law and its provisions in the sense of having the responsibility of taking POWs but saving those persons' lives, that they should act in a humane fashion towards the POWs, treat them humanely, and when they provide security for POWs from these documents, it would follow that those duties have been given over to the security organs and the military police, that they are in charge of providing security and all the other stipulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your expert report, you put forward your opinions about that and substantiate them with a number of MUP documents and police documents for the crossing of borders, and they relate to the period of May and August of 1995, from May to August, and I'm referring to paragraph 4.22 of your report, and the documents are contained in the footnote, in footnote 37, in fact. Now, I'd just like -- no, footnote 57. I meant -- misspoke. Thank you. I'd like us to go through three documents that are characteristic, the first of which is 4D435 [Realtime transcript read in error, "4D35"], and it is in tab 38 of your set. Those are the minutes about the handover and takeover of persons and money between the police station for the border crossing control at Ljubovija -- I'm sorry, the number is 4D435 of the document, 4D435, and the date of the document is the 26th of July, 1995. In your set, as I said, it's to be found in tab 38. I think you have the document in front of you. What can you tell us about this document? What kind of document is this?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the minutes about the transfer of people and money between the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia and the same ministry of Republika Srpska. Specifically, it deals with the border control police station at Ljubovija and the border control police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, does this refer to individuals who potentially can have the status of POWs?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to all intents and purposes, judging by what it says here, that would probably be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next document is tab 39, document 4D434. It is an official note of the police station, the border control police station, with the same date, and the same individuals are mentioned as in the previous document. Tell me, please, what is the link between this document and the previous document in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official persons who signed the previous minutes on behalf of the border control police station in Bratunac, now, with this official note, they recorded the same event and said that they had executed that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's look at the third document in this set. It is tab 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Document 4D433.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is a certificate signed on the one hand by officials from the border control police station in Bratunac, on the one hand, and on the other, the representative of the Bratunac Brigade Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. It is a certificate certifying that the police station is confirming that it handed over the persons and property to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to this and the other documents that you analysed, what were the duties of the Ministry of the Interior vis-a-vis persons who potentially had the status of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these documents, such persons were handed over to the army of Republika Srpska, persons and property, the persons and belongings found on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, I'd like to move on to the fifth chapter of your report, dealing with the procedure for criminal responsibility and disciplinary action for members of the interior in armed conflicts. Let's look at tab 41 of your set and document 4D136, the law governing internal affairs, the consolidated text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We don't have a full translation of this, but relevant of these paragraphs have been translated, and we have hard copies of this for the Court. Oh, we already have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a law that was in force on basic provisions that were in force in 1995, and it contained all the amendments that had been made to date to the law, and I'd like us to look at articles 103 to 107, which means pages 9 and 10 in the B/C/S, and in English, I think we'll be able to find them on the first page, page 1 of the English. Do you have it before you, Article 103? This is about disciplinary responsibility of the MUP officials. In keeping with Article 103, who is in charge of disciplinary measures instituted against members of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Article 103, the person in charge is the minister or an official authorised by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's also look at Article 104. What does this article refer to? Could you please be so kind and tell us?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article regulates or, rather, prescribes the breaches of discipline for which an employee may be held responsible for, but they are not the only ones. It says in paragraph 1, in addition to the violations of duty, there are some other violations that may be constituted violations of duties, and then he goes on to list 11 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now go back to Article 54 of this law, just for the illustration and to see whether this is the only article of this law which deals with the issue of criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to Article 54 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It is page 6 on B/C/S on e-court. You have in front of you Article 54, don't you? But just for the article to appear on e-court, I had to mention the page number. It is page 6. You had an occasion to look at this law. Is this the only paragraph or, rather, article of this law that deals with the issue of criminal responsibility, the criminal responsibility of the members of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Article 54 lists or, rather, says that in case criminal proceedings are instituted in addition to other proceedings for the use of firearms or other means of coercion, the ministry shall be duty-bound to provide such an employee with adequate legal assistance or legal aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I have two somewhat broader questions with regard to the criminal and disciplinary responsibilities. Could you please explain the difference between disciplinary responsibility as opposed to the criminal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference arises from the type of crime or transgression that the person is being held responsible for. Criminal responsibility arises from the commission of an act of crime, whereas disciplinary responsibility arises from breaches of discipline. We are talking about two completely different types of transgressions and two completely different types of proceedings to establish somebody's guilt or responsibility. When it comes to crimes, crimes are punished by sentences or convictions, which is not the case in disciplinary cases. That's why the proceedings in disciplinary cases are more lenient. Disciplinary proceedings are not hardly for courts but, rather, in the ministry itself within the organ of executive power, and there are other differences, but these would be the most important ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I believe we've heard enough about that. I would like us to look at Article 5(6) of your expert report, which deals with reporting. Paragraph 5, item 6 of your expert report. I apologise, paragraph 5, item 6. Very well. This item refers to the notion of reporting and commission of a crime. You define this duty and this issue as defined in your report. What -- in other words, what is understood by the term of "reporting of a crime"? Are there any situations when the failure to report a crime constitutes a crime in its own right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In criminal -- in the criminal legislation of the former SFRY, this issue was regulated in the same way. We are talking about a classical crime of a failure to report a crime. To this very day, when new laws have been passed in the state that has been created and contains all the elements that are necessary, this provision is very much the same as it was before. This means that that obligation still exists for all the citizens only in terms of the gravest of crimes; and for the authorised officials, that obligation is somewhat further-reaching. The authorised officials, according to the legislation of the former SFRY, were duty-bound to report crimes for which a sentence envisaged by the law was five years imprisonment or longer, which are prosecuted ex officio. The citizens were always duty-bound to report only the gravest of crimes for which the envisaged penalty was death penalty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What are the forms of reporting of a crime?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legislation has not envisaged any particular form of reporting of a crime. It can be a verbal complaint or a written complaint. Both would suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just a few more questions to end this part of my examination-in-chief. What conditions have to be met for a report of a crime to be complete and considered to be duly filed?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A crime is reported, i.e., the report thereof has been duly filed if that report, irrespective of its form, is filed with either the authorised or non-authorised state body.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can this also be applied to the officer in the Ministry of the Interior of a unit engaged in combat and resubordinated to the unit in whose zone of responsibility they are deployed?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may be applied to all authorised officials, for example, the provision of Article 199 of the Penal Code of the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, which spoke about the failure to report a crime, truth be told, only in terms of authorised officials. At the same time, the provision of the republican law - and I'm referring to the law of the socialist republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in its Article 185 - spoke about citizens in its first paragraph and about authorised officials in its second paragraph. I repeat, these were typified provisions in the criminal case of all the republics and autonomous provinces, and they could be found more or less in the same form with some possible linguistic and style -- and differences in style. The elements were the same, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Dr. Ristivojevic. I have no further questions for you in this examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Dr. Ristivojevic.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Zivanovic, and I appear on behalf of Vujadin Popovic in this case. I will kindly ask you to answer some questions with regard to your report and with regard to your testimony that we heard the day before yesterday and earlier today. I will start with last things first, and that is the Law on Military Courts; to be more precise, it's Article 56. This is P420, page 9 in the B/C/S version and page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, you said that this provision of the law, the powers and authorities that the MUP had in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedures have been transferred to the security organs and the military police. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Law on Criminal Proceedings, MUP organs had some duties and authorities, and they exercised those in the -- and it is the military police organs and the security organs who exercise the same duties before the military courts or the organs of military judiciary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that they exercised these duties before military courts, are you referring to the pre-trial stage or the trial stage?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation is that all these duties and rights that the MUP organs have, according to the Law on Criminal Proceedings, are transferred on to the security organs and the organs of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask you to read, i.e., to help us read the provision. I would skip bullet points 1 and 2. For a better understanding, I am talking about Article 56, paragraph 2, bullet point 3, which reads: "The duties and authorisations of the organs of the Ministry of Internal Affairs by security organs of the army of Republika Srpska and the military police within the prescribed -- the main activity."

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell me whether this means that they discharge these duties and authorities that would normally belong to the MUP only within the their own purview or, as you've told us, i.e., as I've understood it, that all the authorities are transferred on to the organs of security and military police?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
