utterances.text: Within their remit, which is defined by the rules [Realtime transcript read in error, "roles"] of service of both of these organs, and I've looked at both of these, and I've established that in principle they covered the authorities, the Ministry of the Interior, in criminal proceedings. I did notice some minor differences; for example, the Rules of Service of the Military Police do not provide for the authority of the military police to order a 72-hour custody, but I can see that in the Rules of Service of the Security Organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just for a better understanding, it seems that we have a minor error in the transcript. On page 44 line 24, it says "roles of service" whereas I believe that you said "rules of service"?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just see. Yes, it is rules of service. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does it imply that the organs of the interior still maintain the powers that go with -- without the scope of the responsibility of military police?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that could be construed in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now tell me, how did you establish the scope of responsibility - and I'm going to ask you now only about security organs; we are not talking about military police at the moment - how did you establish what their scope of responsibility was within which these powers were deferred under this law?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Rules of Service of Security Organs, that is how I established the scope of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you have quoted a provision that relates to the fact that security organs participate in preliminary criminal proceedings, if you'll recall that, or if you can define for us this scope? It could be more convenient for us rather than reading the whole provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe we can have some assistance from my learned colleague. If he's referring to certain provisions, I believe it would be fair just for all of us to follow what particular -- what particular provision he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not referring to any particular provision at this moment. I am just asking the expert witness to tell us briefly what is the scope of responsibility of security organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As item 7 of the rules --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, you said you were asking a general question, and then the witness responded with a specific reference to item 7 of the rules, and I'm just wondering if we could at least identify what rules that he is referring to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Rules of Service of Security Organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at this rule. That's Prosecution exhibit P407. I think it's on page 7 or 8 in B/C/S and on page 8 in English, if I am not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you referring to this item? In English, it's on the previous page. It starts on page 7 and then continues on page 8. Can I now ask you to look at page 5 of these rules in B/C/S and page 6 in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I don't see we have -- I think we're going to have it shortly. It's page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that Chapter 1 of the Rules on the Service of Security Organs refers to their competence and that it defines their scope of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's entitled "The Competence and Task of Security Organs."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The first part speaks about the competence. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the next page in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now we can see the B/C/S version, and it says here that the tasks of security organs are defined herein below. Do you agree with me that the competence of security organs is one thing and the tasks of security organs is something different?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you that -- that these two notions differ in the name. One is called "The Tasks," and the other is called "The Competences." However, by interpreting the task, I am not part of the competence or, in other words, that the tasks are, strictly speaking, divided from the competences or separated from the competences. I do not share that opinion, and I would like to refer you to the title of this chapter, which puts both competences and the duties in one sentence. By a systemic interpretation of this law and its contents, my conclusion would be that such strict division cannot exist and that one cannot say that the tasks do not stem from the competences. I couldn't accept that. I would, rather, say that we are dealing here with two notions of different levels or degree of generality. The second one is more specific and is incorporated in the first one, which in my view is at a higher of level of generality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your answer, can we now look again at the competences of security organs and to see to what extent the competences differ from the tasks and to what extent this is just an elaboration of some general principles? Therefore, let us look at the previous page in both versions of the documents. You see that under item 1, and you can read it out loud if you prefer that, it says here that -- under item 1: "The competences encompass the duties of state security issues that are placed within their competence and which are aimed at undermining and toppling the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia and threaten the country's security. If such an activity is carried out in the armed forces or against the armed forces from within the country or from abroad, and also for the purposes of detecting and preventing activities aimed at breaching the secrecy of the plans in preparation of the armed forces the country's Defence..."

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are reading item 1 of the competences?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent. Now, if you look at item 6 of the task, you will read more or less the same, detecting and finding the activities aimed at undermining, et cetera, and it ends, in other words, what I said previously by a systemic interpretation of this document. I understand the task to be an elaboration of competence. We are dealing with two notions of different degrees of generality. For that reason, they are in the same chapter because the latter is the elaboration of the former. That is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned item 6, can you please look at the sentence that -- the very beginning of item 6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we please now go back again one page. That is B/C/S, page 6, and English, page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It says here: "Security organs are responsible for..."

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How do you understand this in view of the tasks listed below including the one that you have just quoted?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we've been responsible for, if you make a linguistic analysis, is that means that somebody is responsible for the execution of these tasks. It is their duty and obligation. Let's say that would be the interpretation of the language used in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can we now move to the next page and look at item 7 that you mentioned and see if we can make certain distinctions in the way that you interpret it.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the way I interpret it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Item 7, I think that on the previous page in English, it says: "The security organs take part..." First of all, we had item 6 stipulating their responsibilities, and now item 7 says: "The security organs take part in the following..." Do you see any substantive difference between the two? If you do, can you explain to us how you understand that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us start from the purely linguistical meaning of the word "taking part in." That means that they participate or take part in the tasks listed herein below from (a) to (f).

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go back to the competences of security organs, can you identify any of these tasks in which security organs participate within their competence?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "... explicitly that they take part in the protection and prevention of serious crimes ..." For example, proposing measures of security and self-protection. Let me just find where the "self-protection" is. 6 -- 3, item 2 says that within law they have the duty, item 2, within their competence they are obliged to provide assistance to self-protection, subject 7(d) --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are to embark on a detailed analysis, and we might draw a number of conclusions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Either I or you draw the attention of the witness to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You have quoted these provisions within the competences, and you mentioned that they provide certain assistance in self-protection, et cetera. Under item 1, their scope of responsibility and competences is stipulated; however, I am interested in something else. You have given us a linguistic interpretation of the word "responsible for." Are you aware that that has a certain meaning in military terms? Does it have any significance where the security organs are responsible or where they participate?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the question whether there is any military document stipulating and defining these two terms?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I am asking you whether you are aware that these two terms have military indications and, hence, military consequences. If something is stipulated for a subject or an entity to be responsible for or on the other hand just to participate in, is there any difference?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean between being responsible for and taking part in. I believe that there could be a difference between the two, but can you please tell me more closely what you're asking me about. If I understood you correctly, you're asking me whether there was any military law defining these two terms, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't want to -- if you don't know about any such documents, I am not insisting on it.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else. Do you know whether these tasks that we have seen under item 7, are these tasks carried out by security organs above by somebody's orders, or do they do that on their own initiative and independently? If you don't know, please say so. I am not going to insist on this.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to some internal relations in the army, who is issuing order to whom, and whether there are any military rules defining this matter; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You know, I am interested to hear how you understand this provision and how it was reflected in your expert report. However, I'm not insisting on going into specific regulations governing this matter.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I included it in my report in the way I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing. Do you believe that those who drafted these laws, i.e., the military courts, when you look at Article 56 where it says that the MUP tasks are to be carried out by the military police and army of Republika Srpska within the prescribed competence, if we omit the word "tasks" and if they are, according to this definition, separate from the competence --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we just briefly make sure about Article 56 that my learned colleague is referring at. Of what particular law or rules or whatever is he talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do apologise. I forgot to state that it is Article 56 of the Law Governing Military Courts that I'm referring to, para 2.3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood your question, and my answer is this: I think that the legislator here in this particular case had no need to mention both concepts for the reasons I've already stated, and that is that I think that we are dealing with two terms, different levels of generality of which one is contained in the other, subsumed in the other, and the second one is an elaboration of the first one. In other words, it is my opinion that the word "tasks," as you put it, has not been omitted for any particular purpose, that the military organs, organs of the military police, do not have the tasks that are provided for in the Rules of Service in Criminal Proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we just have a 65 ter number. A lot of these regulations have very similar titles, and to save us all running through several regulations looking for Article 56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And could they just slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Law is a very complicated matter. So let's slow down a little bit, and I think the point made by Mr. Haynes is a very valid one. Of course, the 65 ter number is there, but in order to be able to follow better during the testimony itself, I think it's better if you refer to the 65 ter number, too, and that applies across the board to everyone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The 65 ter number for this particular document is P420.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ristivojevic, we're going to dwell on this Law Governing Military Courts for a while longer, and in order to do that, let's look at another provision of the law, which is Article 65. What I'm interested in is this: In light of your expert report and your analysis and findings --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd like us to look at page 10 of the B/C/S and page 9 of the English version going on to page 10 thereto.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You've read Article 65, have you?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you then please tell me, what role does the organ of security have in the tasks set out as being every superior officer's duty to carry out?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in Article 65, the superior officer is duty-bound to take certain steps, to take on certain obligations and duties, which naturally come before a criminal act is reported, once he learns of such a criminal act having been committed. In my opinion, they are similar to a certain extent to the duties and obligations governing criminal proceedings. But in this case, they do not emanate strictly from a criminal procedure but are based on logic, I think. So if a superior officer has the duty of reporting a crime that has taken place, that it's quite natural and normal that he would seek as much information about that crime before he reports it. Now, the superior officer won't always have a clear-cut situation in front of him, that is to say, a crime and all the pertinent elements so that he can hand them over to the military prosecutor in a complete set, so to speak. So I suppose or I interpret Article 65 as applying to a situation in which the superior officer has suspicions of a crime and doesn't know everything -- all the details of it. So I think he does have the responsibility to inform himself about the crime as Article 65 stipulates and then to go on and fulfill his duty of reporting the crime. But I do not think that these are duties and obligations which are strictly enumerated in the Law Governing Criminal Procedure or, rather, let me put it this way: I do not think that Article 65 expressly introduces the duty of each superior officer to conduct an investigation in the sense of the provisions of the Law on Criminal Procedure. I think that that is set out in Article 64. That task is given to the investigating judge of a military court as Article 64 stipulates.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's quite clear because here it just says that he should take steps to, not to conduct an investigation. So it says the -- every superior officer is obliged to take steps to, et cetera. Now, tell me, what is the situation like or does this law in article -- have you found an article in the law which in fact states that the superior officer is duty-bound to take into custody anybody looking at this Law Governing Military Courts? If a person is found in the act of committing a crime, is the superior officer duty-bound to arrest that person, or if that person holds other people's lives in jeopardy, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Article 65, I do see that it allows for that possibility because it says to take action to prevent the perpetrator from going into hiding or fleeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at Article 68 in that regard.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does Article 68 define this in more precise terms?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because it takes on the measures stipulated in Article 65 and goes on to define them more precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd now like us to look at another document. It is the Law on the application of the Law Governing Military Courts or the Law Governing the Military Prosecutor's Offices During a State Of War, 4D525.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Prost is drawing my attention that it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this time, this will be the lunch break, so we'll have one hour restarting at 1.30. Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Good afternoon. Good afternoon, everyone. Just a couple of short preliminaries that Mr. Gosnell and I have on some matters. If the Prosecution could seek your permission to reply to the Borovcanin motion on SDS minutes on -- by November 18th, which is the due date for the large joint motion on a similar topic. The SDS minutes motion is due on Monday. The bigger joint motion is due November 18th, and they are very closely related, I think, and so it would be helpful if we could just respond one time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection to that, Mr. Gosnell?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: No objection from our side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We'd ask for exactly the same leave as the Prosecution. We will respond to the motion -- the joint motion on the 18th -- by the 18th of November if given permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that fine with everybody? Okay. Judge Kwon? You have no problem. No, no, permission granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just one additional preliminary, Mr. President. This is to advise the Chamber that we are withdrawing two witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just let me follow you because I have the -- okay. We have Josipovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- Jovic -- and Jovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: And -- Professor Jovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We are in discussions with the Prosecution as to how to deal with the Jovic report. We believe we can deal with it in a fashion that won't involve calling him as a witness. In fact, we're committing to that now, so we are withdrawing those two witnesses. So Professor Ristivojevic is our last oral witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ristivojevic, we stopped off discussing the law and application of the law governing military courts and the Law on the Military Prosecutor's Office During a State of War, and that was exhibit 4D525.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So may we look at the second page of that document -- well, we can see the first page, too, but go on to the second. In fact, what I am interested in is Article 2 -- or, rather, para 2 of that article and you've already discussed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think you said, if I understood you correctly and please correct me if I'm wrong --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That -- Article 2, please. We're dealing with Article 2, so may we have that pulled up on e-court on the previous page, I believe. Article 2. Yes, it's there in the English. We've got that, and we now have it in the B/C/S. No? I don't -- no, that's not the right one. Here we have it in Serbian. Article 4, para 2, and it's on the second page in the B/C/S. That's fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you said that this provision excludes the authority of the Ministry of the Interior and the authorisations that they usually have under the Law on Criminal Proceedings when it comes to crimes that come under the jurisdiction of the military courts, but the others are exempt, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the Law on the implementation of the Law on Military Courts and the Law on the Military Prosecutor's Office during a state of war? This is a new one. We haven't discussed that yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think we did bring it up on page 18 and 19.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see. So you're not referring to our discussion; you're referring my statement, my report? Well, if you're referring to Article 4...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the first and second paras of Article 4 state that the military prosecutor shall have the authority vested in -- by law in the public Prosecutor, and in criminal proceedings for criminal acts falling under the jurisdiction of the military Court, the security organs have that. And in my opinion, it repeats what the Law Governing Military Courts states; that is to say, it establishes their relationship within the frameworks of the Law on Criminal Proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's try and make this clearer. Can you tell us whether that means in your opinion that the organs of the interior retain their authority and competences and that the security organs of the military police are just given some of their -- passed on some of their obligations?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Article 4 states what the military prosecutor has a right to, there is a military prosecutor given the Law on Criminal Proceedings, and on the other hand the military police and its jurisdictions. So they are given those authorisations. So the law in fact repeats what it's already said but deals with a state of war, and the previous article, Article 56, refers to regular situations, peacetime, and this one addresses a state of war, in my opinion, that is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you speak a little slower because we seem to be overlapping.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and speak slower, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 4 of this law states the following: That in proceedings before military courts during a state of war and the duties that the public Prosecutor would be performing is now performed by the military prosecutor, and those duties that would fall to the organs of the Ministry of the Interior are now -- now fall to the military police organs and security organs. In other words, what holds true before military courts when there's no war on will hold true for military courts when there is a state of war. The same would apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's read out para 2 now. Let's leave the first paragraph relating to the military prosecutor out for the moment. As far as I can see, it says the following: "In criminal proceedings for criminal acts falling under the jurisdiction of the military courts, the security organs of the army of Republika Srpska and the military police shall have all the authority vested by" -- I'm afraid I can't see the rest of the text there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next paragraph [In English] B/C/S. [Interpretation] We have it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat. "In criminal proceedings for criminal acts falling under the jurisdiction of the military courts, the security organs of the army of Republika Srpska and the military police shall have all the authority vested by law in the organs of the interior during a state of war."

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand that by this provision the security organs are given the authorities that the organs of the interior normally have during a state of war. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the Law on Criminal Procedure in a state of war, you remember that we talked about that, the application of this law during a state of war narrowing down some deadlines and eliminating right to some legal remedies. You remember that we have spoken about that. Here, the legislator talks about the authorities of the regular courts in a state of war and draws a parallel between the crimes for which the military courts are authorised and the duties of organs in a state of war. There is a logic there, and I don't see a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the organs of the interior have certain authorities, not only under the Law on Criminal Procedure but also under the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you will find this in Articles 41 to 52 of the Law on Internal Affairs. What I'm trying to say is this: Regular courts don't cease to exist or operate during a state of war; hence, this provision and that's why he speaks about the authorities of the Ministry of the Interior during the war, because all the courts operated during the war. This does not exclude the existence of regular courts or their work during a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the application of the Law on Military Courts?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there is no particular criminal procedure that is applied by military courts, and that's why by Article 4, the legislator drew a parallel with this because there is just one criminal procedure that is valid before regular courts and military courts in the state of war. This is my interpretation. I am not saying that you do not have a different interpretation. Don't get me wrong. I am not trying to deprive anybody of their right to a different opinion, but this is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, do you draw a conclude from this provision that the security organs are being given even those competences and authorities that the organs of the interior have even outside the state of war?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside of the state of war? How shall I put it? Given -- just bear with me. I need to think. I believe that the organs of the interior under the Law on Criminal Procedures have powers outside a state of war when there is no war. These powers arise from this Law on Military Courts, and I'm talking about the military police and the organs of security. This Article 4 speaks about the same courts only functioning under the state of war. That's the way I understand this provision. That's how I understand this law. In my view, this speaks about the Law on Criminal Procedure under the state of war, and this law differs slightly from the Law on Criminal Procedure. There are very slight differences there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the powers as they are provided for herein during the state of war also apply to the powers that are prescribed by the law on the application of the Law on the Interior during a state of war. We have already spoken about that law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. This is 1D -- this is 1 -- 413. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that these two laws speak about same powers at all. In the Law on the Application of the Law on Internal Affairs Under the State of War, a possibility is given for the police units to be used in combat, and the Law on Criminal Procedure is something different. These are two different things. As I was reading, the Law on Internal Affairs Under the State of War, I did not notice any special powers of the police in the criminal proceedings in a state of war. This law speaks only about the application, i.e., the use of the police units in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Maybe it would be good if we could clarify the term "criminal proceedings." Could you please explain, under our laws and regulations, what is the meaning of criminal proceedings; i.e., could you please explain or give us the precise moment when the criminal proceedings begin, i.e., from which moment on would this provision be applied?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From which moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It says in the criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can my colleague be more specific about which particular rule he's talking about, which particular article he's talking about. I am having problem following what my colleague is referring at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am sure Mr. Zivanovic will comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is the same article 4, paragraph, second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on this page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, this applies to all the powers that in criminal proceedings belong to the Ministry of the Interior. So we are talking about Article 148 dealing with pre-trial proceedings as well as with the articles applying to trial stage. The organs of the interior and the military police organs can be compared to see what powers belong to whom. I did it only superficially, and I notice that the military police organs did not have the right to military custody of 72 hours arising from Article 96, but both can deprive from freedom a person who is suspected of having committed a crime. I don't see any difference in Article 4 between the two, so whatever exists under the law on criminal proceedings, in criminal proceedings before military courts under -- in a state of war is -- are powers that belong to the security organs and the military police. This is my interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you believe that this provision does not apply only to criminal proceedings but also pre-trial proceedings?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would now kindly ask you to look at the law which you have already mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The exhibit number is 4D413. This is the Law on the Application of the Law on Internal Affairs During a State of War. I believe that we can -- I believe that this is on page -- I apologise, if you could just bear with me. I believe it's page 6, but I'm not sure. Page 4 in e-court. [In English] English version, fourth page. Previous page, third. That's page 8, English page 8 -- 7 -- 9, 9. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ristivojevic, looking at Article 2, may we conclude that the provisions of the Law on Internal Affairs and provisions of other laws and regulations that regulate internal affairs are also applied during a state of war unless provided for differently by this law?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at Article 5.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There are some measures here, which the ministry may take.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, are these some powers that might be applied in preliminary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of these measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Limiting or banning movement of assemblies of people in certain public areas, limiting or banning public gatherings, limiting or banning crossing at certain localities, introducing different regimes of traffic for certain vehicles. I am reading. Just a moment. Yes. Some may be applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at bullet point 10, for example, banning of movement of persons liable for military service without the appropriate permit issued by the military command. This looks like one measure that the Ministry of the Interior applies. Does this belong to the scope of powers that we have just discussed, that the organs of the interior do exercise during a state of war?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is something that a member of the Ministry of the Interior may apply, a ban on movement and similar things. These are some limitations or restrictions of the rights and freedoms that apply to people, and they are applied by the Ministry of the Interior. At least, that's how I understand this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I am now going to move on to another article that you have already spoken about, which is Article 14 of this same law.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this article applies to the use of police units in combat. First of all, I wanted to ask you whether you think that this provision of Article 14 excludes the possibility for police units to be used independently, i.e., not to be resubordinated to the VRS while participating in combat?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, those police units which are used in combat may be used only as units resubordinated to the army of Republika Srpska, and they are resubordinated to them in order to be engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, what is the significance of paragraph 2 of this article where it says that these police units shall be under the direct command of a commander who is a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means - in my opinion, at least - that -- the interpretation of the wording is very clear. The word "direct command" means that they should be commanded by a commander who is a member of the police, of the MUP. I don't see any need for me to provide any other interpretation. I believe that the wording is clear enough. The words "direct command" speak for themselves. This is their first in-charge who is a member of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you understand it as something that should be done or must be done?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In continuation, it reads that: "For the period of resubordination to the army, they maintain their formation and cannot be disintegrated or separated."

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain this? What is the significance that you see in this provision?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, that means that members of a specific police unit cannot be separated and attached to other units - for example, military units - but rather, the unit should be used in combat area in its, what we call, initial formation. That is how I read this. That is to say, you cannot take a police unit and assign two members to one unit, three members to another unit, et cetera. Instead, the unit must be used in its original form.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This paragraph also says that this refers only during the period of their resubordination to the VRS. Do you understand this as something that necessitates a definition of the duration of resubordination of MUP units to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean that an order must precisely specify the period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. You can define a period of time in different ways.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I read it, I would say, pursuant to Article 3, that these units will take part in combat activities. So I understand it that they are resubordinated for as long as combat activities are in progress, and that is in compliance with the task that they had been given of taking part in combat. Once there are no combat activities and their engagement is terminated or fulfilled - I don't know what the proper military term is - I understand it that they would go back to their home base, so to speak, and that is to the Ministry of the Interior. But please do not take my word for granted. When I am using these military terms, I am not sure how you say and you would term the end of combat operations in proper military wording.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to remind you once again to keep it slow, please, because I think we are having problems with the transcript. Can we now look at paragraph 3 of this article, which reads that: "Police units resubordinated to the army of Republika Srpska in a certain zone shall be used only for combat tasks established in advance by the commander-in-chief or the Minister of the Interior." Do you understand this to mean that this provision explicitly directs a limited use of these units, i.e., that they may only be used within combat tasks that had been pre-set?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that one could construe it in that way. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at Exhibit 57. That's Prosecution Exhibit 57. It's an order dated the 10th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, you believe that this order suggests that this unit has been resubordinated to the Drina Corps of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me now, do you see anywhere in this order that it has been resubordinated to anyone?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you're asking me. I do not see this specific word "resubordinate" after reading this order, as you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, under item 5 of this order, it states that the unit commander is "obliged upon their arrival at the destination to make contact with the Corps Chief of Staff General Krstic." Would you understand this part as an order to effect resubordination?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I would interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see a definition in this order of a specific combat task?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see it in the preamble of the order, and that's a combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you overrule -- rule out the possibility for this unit to be used independently concerning that we are talking here about combat activities?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you rule out the possibility, although I think you already answered this, for this unit to be used in combat operation only by being resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is how I understand the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to ask -- show you an order 1D316 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not sure whether it's in e-court already. If it's not, I would like this -- to show the document to the witness. It's 1D316.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe we can clarify the transcript. I believe that there is some ambiguity in the question and the answer that the witness gave. So can my colleague, please, go again through question which was on page 69, line 11. Because the answer was "Yes, this is how I understand the law," and line 15 -- right here on line 15 to line 17, this -- the way the question is posed, and the answer could cause some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can put the same question to you, but I think you did understand it.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Please ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you rule out the possibility for a police unit to be used in combat operations without being resubordinated to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the Law on Internal Affairs in a State of War, only two kinds of units are being established for combat operations and are being used in such a way that they become resubordinated to a military unit in which the zone of responsibility they execute a combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to show you a very short order. It hasn't been translated, and it's not in e-court, so you're going to see it on ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There is no translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I hear that this is in e-court, 1D316.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For that number, we have the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think you will be able to see it on your screen as well. This is an order dated the 30th of March, 1995. It's addressed to the special police brigade command, and it says that the first detachment of the special police of Jahorina be dispatched to carry out a combat task in Konjevic Polje, i.e., to fight the infiltrative, subversive, and terrorist groups. In paragraph 2, it is stated that the police forces staff of the public security centre Zvornik shall control and run the entire MUP forces in the course of carrying out a combat task on the Zvornik-Vlasenica road in order to cut off this road, and --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat. In order to cut off the road and preclude a possible passage of Muslim units from Srebrenica. And in paragraph 3, it says, The centre for training of service dogs will give two -- two guide dogs and two service dogs to the 1st detachment of the special police. I understand that this police unit was sent to take part in combat activities without it being resubordinated to the VRS. Do you understand it in the same way?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you how I understand it. I see that the police forces staff is going to run the forces during the execution of the task. The order does not specify who is in command of these units. They received this order from the Minister of the Interior. I do not see which army unit they are subordinated to, and I don't see who is commanding this unit. It's not written in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: How do you read this term "managing" or "running the entire MUP forces during the combat task"? Can this be done without a command function?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not an expert in expert terminology and expert rules. All I know is what an ordinary and average person who served in the army knows, but I cannot make the distinction between command and control. But it is a fact that the unit to which this police unit is subordinated is not identified -- or, rather, resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it would be fair towards the witness to show him Article 13 of the Law on Implementation of the Law on Internal Affairs. It's 4D413, Article 13, second section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you going to do that, Mr. Zivanovic, yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what it says in Article 13. That's what it says. Control.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, some police units, when they are sent on assignment, do they have their commander?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When speaking of police units sent out for combat activities, they have a commander who is a member of the MUP. So I can't speak in general terms for the whole of the police force. I am addressing this particular situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you something else now. We have had opportunity to see here in this courtroom - whether you've seen it or not and there's no need for us to bring it up on our screens - but we saw that all the units that were within the framework of the Drina Corps - that is to say who were subordinated to the Drina Corps - on a daily basis sent out regular combat reports and reported to the superior command - that is the Drina Corps - about what was going on that day with respect to combat and combat activities. Now, my question to is this: Have you ever seen a combat report of the special police brigade which was sent to the command of the Drina Corps with contents like that or similar contents?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before -- I believe it's far outside from the scope of his expert report. And furthermore, regarding combat report of the special police to Drina Corps's command, I don't know whether there is this proposition that any sort of report was sent to Drina Corps from the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There is no basis for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's take them one by one. Do you wish to comment --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- or shall we refer it straightaway to the witness and he will tell us whether it's within or without the parameters of his expertise?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The witness testified about the resubordination of special brigade of police to the Drina Corps command, and one of the acts of subordination is reporting to higher command or superior command, and I would just like to have information whether the witness ever seen such a record or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, you would know whether you have seen one such report or not, so if you could provide us with your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Now, in the documents that I reviewed for my expert report, I don't remember having seen anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you ever see that this unit or some other unit, MUP unit, during this operation - that is to say, during this time period, which was the subject of your expertise - did it submit any reports to the Ministry of the Interior or the staff of the police forces or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't think so. I don't think I came across anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I am now going to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a report that the centre for public security for the centre of Zvornik on the 13th of July, 1995, addressed to the MUP of Republika Srpska and the police headquarters in Bijeljina, and you can see that the person is reporting on the combat activities on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, would you focus your attention on paragraph 2 of the document where it says: "We have no cooperation or assistance from the army of Republika Srpska in sealing off and destroying a large number of enemy soldiers, so that a lot of problems can be expected until the operation is completed, because the MUP is working alone in this operation, and both the area and the number of Muslim soldiers are large." Tell me now, please, do you gain the impression from that paragraph that this particular MUP unit that took part on the 13th of July in those actions was subordinated to the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we be more -- can my colleague be more specific about which MUP unit he's referring at? Can this be seen from this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is -- it reads in the second line of the first paragraph: 1st Company of special PJP -- CJB Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And your question was whether I conclude what from this report? That the unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That the unit was resubordinated to the police of Republika Srpska in view of the second paragraph where it says that they are acting alone in this operation and that they are receiving no assistance or cooperation, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can conclude from this report - if I've understood this correctly, that it is a report - is that the police unit in question mentioned in the second sentence, that they have a combat task and that they are alone in carrying it out. Now, whether it was resubordinated or not cannot be seen from this order. All we can see is that they have suffered losses, that they are working alone, that they are receiving no assistance, but not whether they are subordinated or not. Perhaps they received a combat assignment to work on their own. I can't know that. All I can see is what it says in this report here. So I can't really answer your question as to whether or whether they were not resubordinated on the basis of what it says here in this report. This is a report, right? You said it was a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, a letter of this kind -- is this the kind of letter you would send to your superior? Because these are very real problems on the ground that the unit is confronting or confronted on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of the expert report and the expertise of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to ask you just one more thing, and it has to do with the prisoners. You have read a lot of provisions, both military and civilian, and I wanted to ask you in view of the fact that you read the Rules of Service of the Security Organs, as well, and other rules and provisions, whether you can or whether in reading through the Rules of Service of the Security Organs within their remit or within the scope of their tasks, did you find any provision which addresses conduct towards prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Rules for Security Organs, I found no such provision. There is one in the Rules Governing the Military Police, but not in the security organ rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you say you found it there. Did you find it any other legal provision that you read while preparing your expert report?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I don't think that I found the mention of security organs in any of the laws. Perhaps the Law on Defence has this term, refers to that, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Zivanovic. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is John Ostojic, and I represent Ljubisa Beara in this case. I have several questions for you. Unfortunately, I don't believe I'll be able to finish today, and thank you for your patience. Sir, first, I want to know if you have a distinction in the term "combat action" or "task" versus "combat operation"?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether there is a distinction between combat action and combat operation, is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, not really. Actually, in your report you use, if you look on 22 -- on Section 21, actually, you use the term "both combat tasks" and "combat activities," and I just don't know if you make a distinction between the two.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't make a distinction. And I read -- I'm reading Article 12, which talks about combat tasks, and Article 13 refers to combat activities. So I am not well-versed in military terminology, so -- and I'm not sure whether the two concepts have different meanings in military terminology. I don't distinguish between that myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you're not a military expert, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. I couldn't actually refer to myself as a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me understand. What expertise do you have, sir, other than reading the statutes and giving you us your view on what the law or statutes might be?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what the subject of my expertise was, whether it was the legal order, provisions, laws, that kind of thing, handbooks, manuals, and individual legal documents, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, in looking at the introduction section of your report, which is on page 1, you talk about how you're going to discuss the issues and relationships between the VRS and the MUP, and you state that you looked -- reviewed some documents. I don't have the list of the documents, but I did locate your report --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will. Thank you. And I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And are all the documents that you reviewed those that are reflected either in the body or in the footnote of your report, or were there other documents that you reviewed as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean whether I mention -- refer to a document in my report without mentioning it in the footnote? I don't think so. I think all the documents I used are mentioned in my footnotes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me try it this way. Were there any other documents that you reviewed that you did not include or cite in your report?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, I see. Yes. For example, I saw the Law on the Gathering of Information About War Crimes from Republika Srpska, but I didn't consider it to be relevant, for example, for the topic of my expert report because it provides for the obligation that all information on war crimes be handed over to state organs, but that is covered by the criminal code, which states that if you do not inform about crimes, you will be held responsible, so there is an example. And there were documents that I wasn't able to find; for example, there is an order which mentions the rules governing the state security department [as interpreted], which I haven't had a chance to see, which says that the president of the republic enacts a set of rules governing the security organs, but I wasn't able to find that document myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, in looking at your task or in the introduction part at the very least, you talk about issues of relationships between the VRS and MUP, as I said. Did you ask for and did you receive documents from the MUP on or about June and July of 1995 to actually be able to see what the situation was and to apply those facts to the law that we can all basically read ourselves, as you have done for us today. Have you done that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment before you answer the question. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. One small correction for the transcript. It's on page 79, line 11 [sic], "governing the state security organs." This is what the witness said, and I cannot see this in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We'll attend to that in due course. Do you still remember the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you ask that again but be briefer. What did you say? Did I from the ministry what?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll ask the question. Thank you. Did you look at the documents from the MUP sources from June and July of 1995 in order to make an application to your interpretation of the law?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the police. I didn't ask the police for anything. I received it from the Defence team. I received documents that I was supposed to study and analyse. Is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't expect you to go directly to the police, but did you get documents relating to the MUP activities in June and July of 1995 to review from any source?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have some few documents. Perhaps you could specify which you mean. If you mean reports, I didn't see any reports, neither did I receive any reports. Now, if you mean a set of some other documents which relate to the activities of the police or conduct of the police, I didn't receive anything specially along those lines if that's what you have in mind. Nobody provided me with a set of documents from the police station or something like that for me to review and analyse, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go some of the reports a little bit later, but let me ask you this. You mention on 2.2 of your report, and you use the word "independently" and "as an independent unit," and it references, obviously, the 10th of July, 1995, order from Tomo Kovac that you just recently discussed, and I think it's P57.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So if we can just bring that up on the e-court, it might assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you look at this document, you see where it uses the word "independent unit," correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in point 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we know from your report that you have an interpretation of that. Would that have been an appropriate place, if you know, if there was going to be an actual resubordination by the various MUP units to use the word "that they will be resubordinated" as opposed to saying that they're going to be an independent unit as it plainly states?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't arrive at that conclusion on the basis of my interpretation of this order. I said what the word "samostalan" or "independent" meant, independent in relation to the other units of the Ministry of the Interior, and I am reading item 5 as an order to resubordinate to this officer -- that the police unit should be resubordinated to this particular officer. That's how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we'll get into resubordination a little later. But now looking at this document, can you tell us if anyone in the VRS was advised of this order and decision to send out MUP units? Do you see on the top left-hand corner to whom this order was addressed, or in the centre page, I think, with the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the addressees I don't see that. I just see - 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 - 7 instances to whom these was addressed. The command of the special police brigade, staff of -- et cetera, staff of the Vogosca, staff of the -- no, there's is no military unit listed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, does that surprise you at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say whether I am surprised or not. I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. In 2.2 of your report, you also use the word "temporary" as you do often, actually. At 4.21, you use it again, and then you use it basically in your conclusion at 6.3 when you discuss these combat activities, if you will, and I'll let you catch up there.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think in 6.3 you use the word "finished." Now, this assignment is always, in nature, temporary, correct, if a MUP unit was to be resubordinated to a VRS corps or unit?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I understand the Law on the Implementation of the Law on Internal Affair During a State of War. For as long as the combat task is in progress, the unit is resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And because you tell us that it's -- the MUP unit is independent from all the other MUP units, would it be fair, then, that no one from MUP would be able to during these combat activities be involved or order this special MUP unit that was purportedly resubordinated, no one from the MUP can command or give orders to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a compound question. It should be split in at least two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No comment, Mr. President. I think he can understand it, but if the Court wants me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- break it down, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see if it is compound for him or compound --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Involved" or "order" are two different concepts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I think the witness -- we have got an intelligent guy here who can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to repeat again or make reference to the Law on Internal Affairs During a State of War. A police unit is to be resubordinated to a military unit in whose zone of responsibility it is carrying out a combat task. And I understand it, it is being commanded by the unit in whose zone of responsibility it is being engaged in a combat activity. This is how I understand the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, you've used a lots of logic in your report and you have in your testimony. The logical extension, sir, would it not be, that someone from -- let's hypothetically say from the Zvornik public security station, a fellow by the name of Dragomir Vasic, he would not be able to intervene in any of the combat activities, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by the word "intervene," please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can be involved in --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know I said it. Can he be involved in any way, since we've assigned this special unit and there's is a deputy commander, it's been clearly defined which units will be participating in these combat activities. Could someone from a public security station or centre of public security, can they order or send any orders to that special MUP unit that's purportedly subordinated to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I read the law, the resubordinated unit is commanded by the military unit, and I'm repeating this for a third time, in whose zone of responsibility it is carrying out a combat task. So I understand this to mean that this military unit to whom the police unit is being resubordinated is giving it commands in terms of how it's going to carry out its combat task.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we look at 2.7 of your report, and we're kind of moving along, you state: "Such a situation lasts as long as it is required by the combat task for the purpose which the MUP unit has been sent." Then you go on to say: "This MUP unit is practically outside the regular system of command of the MUP." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now -- and I know you talk about in another section in your report about specificity and precision. Is the specificity and precision as to both time and place of the combat activity?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean that it is necessary for a combat activity to be precisely defined? Yes. And.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just find the order. Here it is. An order issued by the president of the Republic in terms that henceforth the main MUP staff should give more precise definition of the engagement of MUP units in combat. It says there had been some problems with regard to the engagement to the engagement of some MUP units. I don't know what problems and difficulties they are referring to. I can only make an assumption, but it's not up to me to do so. However, he is ordering this to be defined more precisely and accurately, and it probably means what specific tasks this unit is going to be engaged in. According to what I saw in this order --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get into that order especially when it comes to -- wait -- I know, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The witness has just referred to certain document. I believe that for the clarity of the record, we should have the number of this document at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's exactly why I was trying to cut him off so we could at least get the date of the document if nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, you were referencing -- you said you found an order, and it was an order issued by the president of the republic, and then you go on to give your opinion on it. Just give us the date of that document or if you have an exhibit number in the top right-hand corner, that might help us all follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in a situation where the goal of the combat activity ceases, is it that point in time that the special MUP unit is no longer resubordinated to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of the law is that resubordination lasts as long as the combat task lasts. In my view, at that point resubordination should cease, and the unit should return to its regular police duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that's the way I read it, as well, sir. Well, the task here that you testified about as reflected on the 10th of July, 1995, order, which is I think is P57, is clearly defined, is it not? That's in the introductory paragraph before the words "I hereby order".

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the task that's clearly defined there is to "crush the enemy offensive." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, sir, do you know that as of July 11th and 12th of 1995, there was no enemy offensive in the Srebrenica sector?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, sir, about the events in Srebrenica. If you'll allow me, maybe I can give you an answer. As for the events taking place in Srebrenica in 1995, I only have the knowledge that every average person following the media has. I really don't know when an enemy offensive started or ended. It should be up to military experts to explain to you and give an answer to you about when an offensive starts and when it ends. As I say, I have the knowledge of an ordinary news reader.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, but, sir, you're giving expert evidence here telling us that a unit was resubordinated to the VRS. You're relying on a document, P57, dated the 10th of July, 1995, and you've read the law, and it's pretty clear that the resubordination, if any, ceases immediately upon the completion of a combat task or assignment, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how I understand the law, i.e., that while a unit is engaging a combat task and was subordinated to a military unit in whose zone of responsibility it is carrying out the task, it is for that period outside of the command system of MUP, and it receives orders from the army. Once the task is completed, the unit returns to the MUP. I honestly cannot tell you in military terms when an enemy offensive starts and when it ends. If that is your question, I believe that you have to put it to a military expert, but please don't take it on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, looking at this P57, there were five specific identified parts of the MUP that were going to participate in this combat activity that was well-defined; and I could read through them, but I think we see them: (a), the 2nd special police detachment from Sekovici; (b), or 2, the 1st company of the PJP special police unit of the Zvornik SJB, but it may be CJB; 3, the mixed company of RSK, which is Republika Srpska Krajina; the fourth one is the RS MUP forces, but those were, were they not, from the Trnovo battlefield, just so we can define it a little clearer, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me just to read it, please. In paragraph fourth, it says, The withdrawal from the Trnovo battlefield shall be done during the night, et cetera, et cetera. So are you asking me whether all these units mentioned under item 2 were in Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just try to get a couple of questions out, and then obviously the last one is the training -- or the company from the training camp on Jahorina, right? Those are the ones listed, and we can read them even though we may not agree to it.
